medical.title: Study: Higher rates of parkinsonism among older adults with autism
medical.summary: Middle-aged and older adults with autism are more likely to have co-occurring parkinsonism than adults without autism or intellectual disability, according to a new study led by George Washington University researchers in the Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences.

medical.title: New study identifies biological mechanism driving therapy resistance in advanced prostate cancer
medical.summary: A multi-institutional collaborative study led by researchers at the University of Chicago and the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center has identified a previously unknown biological mechanism that controls cell identity and treatment resistance in advanced prostate cancer.

medical.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
medical.summary: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday.

medical.title: Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk
medical.summary: Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to a dramatically lower risk of dementia and better cognitive functioning in a study spanning up to 43 years. The benefits appeared regardless of genetic risk, but decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association.

medical.title: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
medical.summary: A surprising discovery reveals how psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, rapidly reshapes the brain by creating new neural connections and strengthening them. Researchers found that the drug behaves differently in healthy and chronically stressed mice, potentially helping repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. Most intriguingly, they identified a way to trigger this brain rewiring without the behavioral response associated with psychedelic effects.

medical.title: A compound hidden in broccoli could help fight a devastating genetic disease
medical.summary: A compound naturally found in broccoli could help fight Friedreich ataxia, a devastating genetic disease that progressively damages the nervous system, by boosting a vital protein and protecting nerve cells. Scientists hope the discovery could lead to an affordable treatment, although clinical trials are still needed to establish its effectiveness in patients.

medical.title: The women’s boxing nights helping abuse survivors
medical.summary: A series of all-female fight nights aims to fund free boxing classes that help women rebuild their confidence after abusive relationships The post The women’s boxing nights helping abuse survivors appeared first on Positive News .

medical.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
medical.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain. Researchers discovered that the benefits may be linked to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP-1, revealing a promising new approach to arthritis relief.

medical.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
medical.summary: A major new study reveals that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and those differences may begin earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children. The discovery could help explain why some autistic people have difficulty recognizing faces and reading emotions.

medical.title: Scientists discover the immune system’s hidden sense of touch
medical.summary: Scientists at McGill University have discovered a surprising new ability of immune cells that could change how we understand long-term immunity. Researchers found that T cells can actually sense how stiff their surrounding tissues are, using these physical signals to help determine whether they develop into long-lasting memory cells that protect against future infections.

science.title: Theory predicting an older universe without dark matter or dark energy passes key cosmological tests
science.summary: An alternative model in which the universe is 26.7 billion years old and needs neither dark matter nor dark energy has held up against several major cosmology tests, according to a new University of Ottawa study. The research, titled "A Big Bang Nucleosynthesis Consistency Test of the CCC+TL Cosmology," is published in the journal Universe.

science.title: Why treating soil acidity crop by crop is no longer enough for prairie farmers
science.summary: To protect their future harvests, Western Canadian farmers need to manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation rather than crop by crop, long-term research from the University of Alberta suggests.

science.title: Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here's how to stay safer
science.summary: For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safely.

science.title: Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station
science.summary: A Pakistani astronaut will join the crew of China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft on a mission that would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing's space station, state media reported Saturday.

science.title: Atlanta's new giant pandas will make their public debut after a 2-year absence
science.summary: Panda lovers are expected to line up Friday at Zoo Atlanta to see a new pair of giant pandas make their public debut.

science.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
science.summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.

science.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
science.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky. The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust. Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.

science.title: Scientists accidentally solve a chemistry mystery that lasted 60 years
science.summary: After more than 60 years of unsuccessful attempts, scientists have finally isolated stable examples of elusive boron-oxygen molecules once considered too unstable to capture. The surprising breakthrough, achieved using relatively simple chemical reactions, could pave the way for an entirely new class of exotic compounds.

environment.title: Amazon mapping shows cacao expansion without deforestation in Brazil
environment.summary: While West Africa clears rainforest for chocolate, Brazilian farmers are reviving degraded pastures.

environment.title: Money laundering complaints target JBS, Barclays over profits linked to illegal deforestation
environment.summary: A coalition of legal and environmental groups has filed money laundering complaints against JBS, the world’s largest meat processor, and 12 financial institutions, investors and advisers, including the U.K. bank Barclays. The complaints allegedly tie JBS profits to illegal deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon. The Transnational Legal Coalition filed 14 complaints with prosecutors and financial […]

environment.title: 3M agrees to pay more than $7 billion to settle ‘forever chemical’ groundwater contamination claims
environment.summary: Chemical manufacturer 3M will pay up to $7.35 billion to settle lawsuits by people who say they were sickened by groundwater contamination from compounds used in firefighting foam and other consumer products. The St. Paul, Minnesota-based company announced the settlement Tuesday. It will pay the money over nine years to as many as 120,000 people […]

environment.title: How Ghana’s new license to sell sustainable timber improves institutions & cooperation (analysis)
environment.summary: When Ghana began its Voluntary Partnership Agreement (VPA) process with the European Union, the attraction was clear. Europe is an important market for Ghanaian timber, international expectations around its legality were changing, and the VPA offered both market access and support for strengthening national forest governance. After a 16-year journey, last year Ghana became the […]

environment.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
environment.summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.

environment.title: A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea and unleashed a 330-foot tsunami
environment.summary: A decades-long mystery beneath the North Sea has finally been solved. Scientists have confirmed that the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was created when a 160-meter-wide asteroid struck Earth roughly 43 to 46 million years ago. The violent collision blasted a towering curtain of rock and water 1.5 kilometers into the air and triggered a tsunami more than 100 meters high.

environment.title: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
environment.summary: Deep inside a high-altitude Chinese cave, scientists discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail that has evolved to live entirely in darkness, marking the first recorded discovery of its kind in China. Named after a faceless mythical creature, the rare species may already be in danger, with researchers finding only three living adults.

environment.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
environment.summary: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

environment.title: “Crawzilla” was huge. Then scientists found an even bigger crayfish
environment.summary: A nationwide search for giant crayfish uncovered a record-breaking Tennessee specimen and a surprising mystery about how big these freshwater creatures can grow. Scientists found that North American crayfish seem to hit a biological size limit, possibly because of their muscles or protective shells.

mix_items.title: Căutăm coleg/ă Responsabil Comunicare și Promovare
mix_items.summary: Când a fost ultima dată când ai simțit că munca ta chiar schimbă ceva? Poate ai creat campanii care au generat mii de vizualizări. Poate ai crescut comunități online, ai scris articole, ai organizat evenimente sau ai construit branduri. Dar câte dintre ele au schimbat cu adevărat viața cuiva? La Fundația Motivation România și la... The post Căutăm coleg/ă Responsabil Comunicare și Promovare appeared first on Fundatia Motivation Romania .

mix_items.title: Study: Higher rates of parkinsonism among older adults with autism
mix_items.summary: Middle-aged and older adults with autism are more likely to have co-occurring parkinsonism than adults without autism or intellectual disability, according to a new study led by George Washington University researchers in the Department of Speech, Language and Hearing Sciences.

mix_items.title: New study identifies biological mechanism driving therapy resistance in advanced prostate cancer
mix_items.summary: A multi-institutional collaborative study led by researchers at the University of Chicago and the Fred Hutchinson Cancer Center has identified a previously unknown biological mechanism that controls cell identity and treatment resistance in advanced prostate cancer.

mix_items.title: Why treating soil acidity crop by crop is no longer enough for prairie farmers
mix_items.summary: To protect their future harvests, Western Canadian farmers need to manage soil acidity across their entire multiyear rotation rather than crop by crop, long-term research from the University of Alberta suggests.

mix_items.title: Diwali celebrations coincide with worsening air. Here's how to stay safer
mix_items.summary: For people across South Asia, especially in northern India, Diwali celebrations coincide with the return of hazardous winter air, raising concerns about how to celebrate safely.

mix_items.title: Pakistani astronaut to board Shenzhou 24 and become the first foreigner on China's space station
mix_items.summary: A Pakistani astronaut will join the crew of China's Shenzhou 24 spacecraft on a mission that would make him the first foreign national to board Beijing's space station, state media reported Saturday.

mix_items.title: US reports highest number of measles cases in 35 years
mix_items.summary: The United States has recorded more than 5,000 cases of measles this year, the highest number in 35 years, according to an official count released Friday.

mix_items.title: Atlanta's new giant pandas will make their public debut after a 2-year absence
mix_items.summary: Panda lovers are expected to line up Friday at Zoo Atlanta to see a new pair of giant pandas make their public debut.

mix_items.title: Drinking 2–3 cups of coffee a day linked to dramatically lower dementia risk
mix_items.summary: Drinking two to three cups of caffeinated coffee daily was linked to a dramatically lower risk of dementia and better cognitive functioning in a study spanning up to 43 years. The benefits appeared regardless of genetic risk, but decaffeinated coffee did not show the same association.

mix_items.title: Scientists discover Europe's ancient forests were nothing like we imagined
mix_items.summary: Scientists have uncovered evidence that Europe was dominated for more than 20 million years by open woodlands, colorful meadows, and large grazing animals, not the dense forests long considered its natural state. The surprising discovery challenges modern reforestation strategies, suggesting that planting thick forests could actually harm the biodiversity conservationists hope to protect.

mix_items.title: Rubin Observatory discovers two hidden companions of the Milky Way. Hundreds more may be waiting
mix_items.summary: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory has already uncovered two previously unknown companions of the Milky Way using preliminary observations covering just 7% of the night sky. The discoveries include an extremely faint galaxy 355,000 light-years away and a star cluster hidden behind cosmic dust. Scientists suspect hundreds of additional satellite galaxies remain undiscovered, and Rubin's powerful telescope could finally bring them into view.

mix_items.title: Magic mushrooms rewire the brain in a way scientists didn't expect
mix_items.summary: A surprising discovery reveals how psilocybin, the active compound in magic mushrooms, rapidly reshapes the brain by creating new neural connections and strengthening them. Researchers found that the drug behaves differently in healthy and chronically stressed mice, potentially helping repair brain circuits damaged by prolonged stress. Most intriguingly, they identified a way to trigger this brain rewiring without the behavioral response associated with psychedelic effects.

mix_items.title: A compound hidden in broccoli could help fight a devastating genetic disease
mix_items.summary: A compound naturally found in broccoli could help fight Friedreich ataxia, a devastating genetic disease that progressively damages the nervous system, by boosting a vital protein and protecting nerve cells. Scientists hope the discovery could lead to an affordable treatment, although clinical trials are still needed to establish its effectiveness in patients.

mix_items.title: Scientists accidentally solve a chemistry mystery that lasted 60 years
mix_items.summary: After more than 60 years of unsuccessful attempts, scientists have finally isolated stable examples of elusive boron-oxygen molecules once considered too unstable to capture. The surprising breakthrough, achieved using relatively simple chemical reactions, could pave the way for an entirely new class of exotic compounds.

mix_items.title: Amazon mapping shows cacao expansion without deforestation in Brazil
mix_items.summary: While West Africa clears rainforest for chocolate, Brazilian farmers are reviving degraded pastures.

mix_items.title: Money laundering complaints target JBS, Barclays over profits linked to illegal deforestation
mix_items.summary: A coalition of legal and environmental groups has filed money laundering complaints against JBS, the world’s largest meat processor, and 12 financial institutions, investors and advisers, including the U.K. bank Barclays. The complaints allegedly tie JBS profits to illegal deforestation in the Brazilian Amazon. The Transnational Legal Coalition filed 14 complaints with prosecutors and financial […]

mix_items.title: 3M agrees to pay more than $7 billion to settle ‘forever chemical’ groundwater contamination claims
mix_items.summary: Chemical manufacturer 3M will pay up to $7.35 billion to settle lawsuits by people who say they were sickened by groundwater contamination from compounds used in firefighting foam and other consumer products. The St. Paul, Minnesota-based company announced the settlement Tuesday. It will pay the money over nine years to as many as 120,000 people […]

mix_items.title: How Ghana’s new license to sell sustainable timber improves institutions & cooperation (analysis)
mix_items.summary: When Ghana began its Voluntary Partnership Agreement (VPA) process with the European Union, the attraction was clear. Europe is an important market for Ghanaian timber, international expectations around its legality were changing, and the VPA offered both market access and support for strengthening national forest governance. After a 16-year journey, last year Ghana became the […]

mix_items.title: The women’s boxing nights helping abuse survivors
mix_items.summary: A series of all-female fight nights aims to fund free boxing classes that help women rebuild their confidence after abusive relationships The post The women’s boxing nights helping abuse survivors appeared first on Positive News .

mix_items.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
mix_items.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain. Researchers discovered that the benefits may be linked to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP-1, revealing a promising new approach to arthritis relief.

mix_items.title: The autistic brain processes faces differently than scientists thought
mix_items.summary: A major new study reveals that autistic children’s brains process faces differently, and those differences may begin earlier than scientists previously thought. Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children. The discovery could help explain why some autistic people have difficulty recognizing faces and reading emotions.

mix_items.title: Scientists discover the immune system’s hidden sense of touch
mix_items.summary: Scientists at McGill University have discovered a surprising new ability of immune cells that could change how we understand long-term immunity. Researchers found that T cells can actually sense how stiff their surrounding tissues are, using these physical signals to help determine whether they develop into long-lasting memory cells that protect against future infections.

mix_items.title: A train was delayed by a solar storm. But something didn't add up.
mix_items.summary: Scientists have cracked a 178-year-old mystery surrounding a train delayed by a solar storm, revealing that the famous incident happened in 1848 rather than 1841. The discovery rewrites the early history of space weather and highlights a threat that still endangers modern power grids, satellites, and communication systems.

mix_items.title: A massive asteroid slammed into the North Sea and unleashed a 330-foot tsunami
mix_items.summary: A decades-long mystery beneath the North Sea has finally been solved. Scientists have confirmed that the Silverpit Crater, buried 700 meters below the seabed, was created when a 160-meter-wide asteroid struck Earth roughly 43 to 46 million years ago. The violent collision blasted a towering curtain of rock and water 1.5 kilometers into the air and triggered a tsunami more than 100 meters high.

mix_items.title: Scientists discover ghostly, eyeless creature hidden in Chinese cave
mix_items.summary: Deep inside a high-altitude Chinese cave, scientists discovered a ghostly, eyeless freshwater snail that has evolved to live entirely in darkness, marking the first recorded discovery of its kind in China. Named after a faceless mythical creature, the rare species may already be in danger, with researchers finding only three living adults.

mix_items.title: Scientists discover a plastic-eating “Pac-Man” enzyme with a surprising secret
mix_items.summary: Scientists have discovered a remarkable “Pac-Man enzyme” that helps bacteria devour certain types of plastic and may offer new hope in the fight against plastic pollution. Researchers found that several biodegradable plastics completely broke down in soil within about a year, while conventional plastic remained largely unchanged.

mix_items.title: “Crawzilla” was huge. Then scientists found an even bigger crayfish
mix_items.summary: A nationwide search for giant crayfish uncovered a record-breaking Tennessee specimen and a surprising mystery about how big these freshwater creatures can grow. Scientists found that North American crayfish seem to hit a biological size limit, possibly because of their muscles or protective shells.
